title: Multi-AZ
subtitle: Intra-region fault domain isolation, synchronous storage replication, and cross-AZ network cost optimization.
keyTakeaways: An Availability Zone (AZ) is one or more discrete data centers with independent power, cooling, and physical networking within a metropolitan region, connected by low-latency (<2ms) dark fiber.
Low inter-AZ latency (0.5ms - 2ms) enables synchronous database replication and consensus quorums (Raft/Paxos) across 3 AZs with zero data loss (RPO = 0) on single-AZ failure.
Cross-AZ data transfer is billed by cloud providers ($0.01-$0.02/GB each way); high-throughput systems use Topology-Aware Routing to keep RPC and cache reads within the local AZ.

sections.heading: Physical Isolation & Synchronous Consensus Across 3 AZs
sections.body: A single data center can fail due to transformer explosions, cooling leaks, or fiber cuts. Cloud regions group 3 or more physically separated Availability Zones (typically 10-100 km apart) so they do not share Flood/Power fault domains, while keeping round-trip network latency under 2 milliseconds.
bullets: Why 3 AZs Instead of 2: Consensus protocols (etcd, Raft, ZooKeeper, Patroni) require a strict majority quorum ($\lfloor N/2 \rfloor + 1$). With 2 AZs, a majority is $\lfloor 2/2 \rfloor + 1 = 2$—meaning if either AZ goes dark, the cluster loses quorum and halts writes! With 3 AZs, quorum is 2, surviving any single AZ loss.

Synchronous Storage Durability: Cloud-native databases (AWS Aurora, CockroachDB) write WAL logs across 6 storage nodes spanning 3 AZs and acknowledge commits once 4 of 6 nodes confirm, achieving RPO = 0 with ~1.5ms write overhead.

Over-Provisioning for N-1 Capacity: In a 3-AZ deployment, each AZ handles 33.3% of traffic. If one AZ fails, the remaining two AZs must immediately absorb 50% each—meaning baseline utilization should not exceed ~60%.

codeSnippet.title: Kubernetes Topology Spread Constraints & Zone-Aware Routing
codeSnippet.code:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: payment-service
spec:
  replicas: 6
  template:
    spec:
      topologySpreadConstraints:
        - maxSkew: 1
          topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
          whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule
          labelSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app: payment-service
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: payment-service
  annotations:
    # Prefer routing traffic to pods within the caller's same AZ
    service.kubernetes.io/topology-mode: Auto

sections.heading: Hidden Cross-AZ Egress Costs & Zonal Affinity
sections.body: While Multi-AZ protects against data center failures, naive round-robin load balancing across 3 AZs means 66% of every microservice hop, Redis read, and Kafka consumer fetch crosses an AZ boundary—incurring bilateral data transfer charges and adding 1-2ms per hop.
bullets: Topology-Aware Service Routing: Configure Envoy / Kubernetes EndpointSlices to route RPCs to healthy pods in the same AZ first, spilling over to peer AZs only when local capacity is saturated or unhealthy.

Kafka Rack-Aware Consumers: Set `client.rack` on consumers and `broker.rack` on Kafka brokers so consumers fetch high-volume partition replicas from the local AZ's follower broker rather than crossing AZs to the leader.

Grey Failure & Zonal Evacuation: Sometimes an AZ suffers partial packet loss rather than total blackout; operators use Zonal Shift to drain traffic away from the degraded AZ via DNS/Load Balancer weights.

tradeOffs.pros: Evenly balances CPU/memory across all instances regardless of uneven ingress distribution per AZ.
tradeOffs.cons: 66% of traffic crosses AZ boundaries, incurring $0.02/GB transfer fees and extra 1ms latency per hop.
tradeOffs.bestFor: Low-bandwidth, CPU-intensive RPC services where even compute utilization outweighs network transfer fees.

tradeOffs.pros: Eliminates cross-AZ network egress charges and shaves 1-2ms per hop across deep microservice chains.
tradeOffs.cons: Can cause hot-spotting if one AZ has fewer healthy pods or receives disproportionate ingress traffic.
tradeOffs.bestFor: High-bandwidth data pipelines, Kafka consumers, distributed caches, and chatty microservice meshes.

interviewTip: Always explain why production stateful systems deploy across **3 AZs** rather than 2: in a 2-AZ setup, if the AZ hosting the primary (or 50% of quorum nodes) loses connectivity, the surviving AZ only has 50% of votes and cannot safely elect a new leader without risking split-brain.
